newsitem.title: TAIWAN: CPC stalls joint oil plan with China.
newsitem.headline: CPC stalls joint oil plan with China.

text.p: Taiwan's state monopoly Chinese Petroleum Corp has stalled a plan for joint oil exploration with China following Taipei's recent calls to tone down economic links with China, a company spokeswoman said on Tuesday.
"We are a state company and we have to comply with the government's policy," the spokeswoman told Reuters.
But she declined to say whether the joint oil exploration plan with China had been cancelled.
"All we can say now is there is no contact at this moment and we do not have plan to hold talks with the mainalnd side in the near future," she said.
Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui said in August that the island needed to review its policy of targeting China as its main market and avoid over-dependence on the mainland for investment.
Various government agencies, including the economics ministry and the Mainland Affairs Council, the island's top policymaking body toward China, made similar comments afterwards.

Chinese Petroleum said in October that it would halt new overseas investments temporarily in response to the economics ministry's call to strengthen local investments, although contracted projects would continue as planned.

Chinese Petroleum signed a landmark pact with Beijing's China National Offshore Corp in July for joint research and preparation for oil exploration between south China's Pearl River delta and the Taiwan Straits.
The accord has been seen as a breakthrough in Taiwan-China relation as Taiwan bans contact of its state firms with China after a civil war separated them in 1949.
The deal was put in the name of Chinese Petroleum's offshore subsidiary, Overseas Petroleum Investment Corp, to avoid violating current restrictions.
